phenomena.claim: Universality/equality of electric charge across matter: the proton-electron charge difference is bounded at |eps_{p-e}| <~ 1e-21 e (same bound for neutron neutrality)
phenomena.source: Bressi et al., Phys. Rev. A 83, 052101 (2011) — abstract fetched and matched 2026-09-23
phenomena.caveat: bound from bulk-matter neutrality (SF6 spherical capacitor), not per-particle spectroscopy

phenomena.claim: No free (isolated, fractionally charged) quarks are observed; only color-singlet hadrons appear in the asymptotic spectrum
phenomena.source: Stage 2: cite PDG free-quark search compilation (e.g. PDG 'Quark Searches' listing) or a canonical Millikan-type/accelerator search review

phenomena.source: PDG 2024 QCD review (rpp2024-rev-qcd.pdf), Fig. 9.5 and surrounding text — fetched at source 2026-09-23; archive: RAI_STRUCTURAL_THEORY_SEARCH Answer 1 lists asymptotic freedom among PREDICTION-grade confirmations

formalism.source: archive: origin/v4:program/REALITY_PICTURE_01.md LEVEL 1 row 'Gauge redundancy (not physical freedom) | SM consistency [T] | forced [T]' — quote confirmed against origin/v4 2026-09-23

formalism.claim: Local (non-Abelian) gauge invariance fixes the interaction structure: gauge fields enter as connections, field strength as curvature, coupling universally to the corresponding currents
formalism.source: Yang & Mills, Phys. Rev. 96, 191 (1954) — abstract fetched and matched 2026-09-23; geometric (fiber-bundle) reading is textbook-standard
formalism.caveat: the bundle dictionary's primary source (Wu & Yang 1975) not independently fetched — see alternative_formulations

formalism.claim: Gauge theories are renormalizable; dimensional regularization preserves gauge invariance through renormalization
formalism.source: 't Hooft & Veltman, Nucl. Phys. B 44, 189 (1972) 'Regularization and Renormalization of Gauge Fields' — INSPIRE record matched 2026-09-23
formalism.caveat: renormalizability here is perturbative; non-perturbative existence is a separate (open) question — see known_disconnects

formalism.claim: Anomaly cancellation is a consistency condition on chiral gauge theory, and the SM's quark+lepton content cancels the gauge anomalies generation by generation
formalism.source: Adler, Phys. Rev. 177, 2426 (1969) (triangle anomaly — abstract fetched 2026-09-23); Bouchiat, Iliopoulos & Meyer, Phys. Lett. B 38, 519 (1972) 'An Anomaly Free Version of Weinberg's Model' — INSPIRE record matched 2026-09-23
formalism.caveat: Bell & Jackiw companion anomaly paper not separately fetched

formalism.claim: Local gauge symmetry cannot break spontaneously (Elitzur's theorem): without gauge fixing, non-gauge-invariant local order parameters have vanishing expectation values
formalism.source: Elitzur, Phys. Rev. D 12, 3978 (1975) — abstract fetched and matched 2026-09-23
formalism.caveat: proved on the lattice for the Abelian case in the source, standard generalization since; consequence: the 'Higgs mechanism' is a gauge-invariantly describable spectrum statement, not literal symmetry breaking

primitives.claim: The gauge group SU(3)xSU(2)xU(1) and the fermion representation content are primitives (inputs) of the SM, not derived
primitives.source: archive: REALITY_PICTURE_01 Q17 minimum input set includes 'SM content + couplings'; LEVEL 3 'SM ──INPUT──▶ 19+ empirical parameters [T] INPUT (not derived)'

derived_objects.claim: Asymptotic freedom (negative beta function) is derived from non-Abelian gauge structure
derived_objects.source: Gross & Wilczek, Phys. Rev. Lett. 30, 1343 (1973) — abstract fetched and matched 2026-09-23

derived_objects.claim: The light hadron spectrum is computed ab initio from lattice QCD with fully controlled uncertainties and agrees with experiment (confinement realized quantitatively in the regulated theory)
derived_objects.source: Durr et al., Science 322, 1224 (2008), arXiv:0906.3599 — abstract fetched and matched 2026-09-23
derived_objects.caveat: numerical continuum extrapolation, not an analytic proof of confinement

derived_objects.caveat: archive grade as recorded: [LITERATURE] (the claim carries no inline [VERIFIED] marker and the document declares itself [LITERATURE]-grade outside [VERIFIED]-marked sections, section 10); the primary citation was independently verified at abstract level for this corpus entry

known_disconnects.claim: Confinement with a mass gap has NOT been derived from continuum 4D Yang-Mills at mathematical rigor
known_disconnects.source: Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize problem 'Yang-Mills existence and mass gap' (official statement by Jaffe & Witten) — claymath.org fetched and matched 2026-09-23
known_disconnects.caveat: lattice strong-coupling argument (Wilson 1974) and numerical evidence (Durr 2008) are strong; the absence is of a rigorous continuum construction/proof

known_disconnects.claim: No rigorous construction of any interacting 4D QFT exists; the structural field routes around this deficit of its own most triumphant physics
known_disconnects.source: archive: origin/v4:RAI_STRUCTURAL_THEORY_SEARCH.md section 8, 'Second-order gap, independently reached' — wording confirmed against origin/v4 2026-09-23
known_disconnects.caveat: the absence itself is community-acknowledged (status of constructive QFT); the 'routes around this deficit' characterization is the archive's reading of the field, not a community statement

known_disconnects.claim: The electroweak transition is a crossover, not first order, at the observed Higgs mass: Sakharov's departure-from-equilibrium condition is absent within the SM gauge-Higgs sector
known_disconnects.source: archive: RAI_STRUCTURAL_THEORY_SEARCH Answer 1, marked [VERIFIED] in the archive at source level — Csikor, Fodor & Heitger (hep-ph/9809291), lattice endpoint m_H = 66.5 +/- 1.4 GeV (SU(2)-Higgs), ~72.4 +/- 1.7 GeV (SM), vs m_H = 125.20 GeV observed
known_disconnects.caveat: exclusion conditional on the LEP bound as recorded; 'no phase transition' means crossover, which is the structural claim
